title: Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI, Google made ‘illegal’ agreement on AI slowdown, says new lawsuit
summary: The lawsuit reportedly argues that the leading AI companies violated antitrust laws when they agreed to coordinate slowdown efforts, and that doing so would reduce the value consumers get for paid AI subscriptions.

title: More Australians to live into their 90s as life expectancy forecast to rise over coming decades
summary: Treasury’s latest intergenerational report projects life expectancy at birth will reach 89 for women and 86 for men by 2066 Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian households will shrink but more people can expect to live well into their 90s, according to the latest update to forecasts of the country’s long-term future. Treasury’s latest intergenerational report, to be published in full on Monday, will project the impact of government policies 40 years into the future. Continue reading...
author: Australian Associated Press and Sarah Basford Canales

title: We’re Not Losing Control of A.I. We’re Giving It Away.
summary: The idea of “pacing the frontier” to ensure A.I. safety has taken hold since the hack of Hugging Face. But as the Opinion columnist Ezra Klein argues, “walking quickly off a cliff is only marginally better than sprinting off one.” In this video essay, he explains how we got here — and what frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI must do to regain control.

title: We’re Not Losing Control of A.I. We’re Giving It Away.
summary: Letting A.I. patrol its own frontier is like asking Jesse James to patrol the Wild West.
author: Ezra Klein, Marie Cascione, Claire Gordon and Rollin Hu

title: We’re Not Losing Control of A.I. We’re Giving It Away.
summary: Artificial intelligence labs are on the verge of handing over the training of A.I. to A.I. We should stop them.

title: A.I. Gone Rogue? Trump Proposes Not New Rules but an ‘A.I. Force.’
summary: The president proposed a follow-up to his Space Force but continued to dismiss worries about A.I.’s pace or potential for harm.
author: David E. Sanger and Tim Balk
